blogDetail.author: Super Admin
blogDetail.lead: In today's digital economy, trust is the currency that powers every online transaction. Understanding how the right safeguards work is the first step toward transacting with complete peace of mind.

body.heading: Why this matters now
paragraphs: Online commerce has never moved faster — and neither have the tactics used to exploit it. Whether you're buying a car, hiring a freelancer, or closing a high-value deal, the moment money changes hands is the moment risk peaks.
That's exactly where a neutral third party changes the equation. By holding funds securely until both sides meet their obligations, an escrow layer removes the leap of faith that fraud thrives on.

body.heading: How the protection works
paragraphs: The flow is simple by design. The buyer deposits funds, the seller delivers, and only once the buyer confirms — or a dispute is fairly resolved — are the funds released. Neither party can walk away with both the money and the goods.
This structure turns an anonymous transaction between strangers into a predictable, auditable process backed by real accountability.

blogDetail.quote: Trust shouldn't be a gamble. It should be built into the transaction itself.
blogDetail.checklistTitle: What a strong escrow layer gives you
checklist: Funds held securely until conditions are met
Clear, documented milestones for both parties
Fair dispute resolution when things go wrong
Full transaction transparency from start to finish
blogDetail.closing: The bottom line: protecting your money online isn't about avoiding transactions — it's about structuring them so both sides can move forward with confidence.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: How Escroc collects, uses, and protects your personal information.

sections.title: Information We Collect
sections.body: We collect the information you give us directly — your name, email address, phone number, and government ID during KYC verification — along with transaction details, wallet addresses, and basic device/browser data collected automatically when you use Escroc.

sections.title: How We Use Your Information
sections.body: Your information is used to process escrow transactions, verify your identity, prevent fraud, provide customer support, and comply with financial regulations. We never sell your personal data to third parties.

sections.title: How We Protect Your Information
sections.body: Sensitive data, including payment details and KYC documents, is encrypted both in transit and at rest. Card payments are processed through PCI-DSS compliant gateways, and we never store full card numbers on our own servers.

sections.title: Sharing With Third Parties
sections.body: We share information only with the payment gateways, banking partners, and compliance providers required to complete a transaction, or when required by law to prevent fraud or protect our users' rights and property.

sections.title: Data Retention
sections.body: We retain account and transaction records for as long as your account is active, and for a further period afterward as required by financial record-keeping regulations, after which the data is securely deleted.

sections.title: Your Rights & Choices
sections.body: You can review, update, or request deletion of your personal information at any time from your account settings, subject to the retention obligations described above. Contact support@escroc.com for any privacy request.

sections.title: Changes to This Policy
sections.body: We may update this policy from time to time. Material changes will be posted on this page and, where required, communicated to you directly.

refund.title: Refund Policy
refund.subtitle: How refunds work for escrow transactions, deposits, and payments.

sections.title: Escrow-Based Refunds
sections.body: Because Escroc holds funds in escrow until both parties confirm a transaction, refunds are primarily handled through the release and dispute flow inside each escrow, rather than a traditional after-the-fact refund request.

sections.title: Buyer-Initiated Disputes
sections.body: If a buyer does not receive the agreed goods or service, they can open a dispute from the escrow's conversation page. Funds remain held securely until the dispute is reviewed and resolved.

sections.title: Seller-Initiated Release
sections.body: Once a seller has delivered as agreed, the buyer approves release of the funds. Sellers may also send a release request when they believe the buyer is satisfied.

sections.title: Payment Gateway Refunds
sections.body: If a transaction is cancelled before both parties confirm, or a payment fails or is duplicated, any amount charged through a payment gateway (card, bank, or crypto) is refunded to the original payment method within 5–10 business days, minus any non-refundable processing fees already charged by the gateway.

sections.title: Non-Refundable Fees
sections.body: Platform service fees and currency-exchange charges already applied to a completed transaction are non-refundable once funds have been released to the seller.

sections.title: How to Request a Refund
sections.body: Contact our support team from the Support section of your dashboard with your transaction ID. We review every request and respond within 2 business days.

terms.title: Terms & Conditions
terms.subtitle: The rules that govern your use of the Escroc platform.

sections.title: Acceptance of Terms
sections.body: By creating an account or using Escroc, you agree to be bound by these Terms & Conditions and our Privacy Policy. If you do not agree, please do not use the platform.

sections.title: Eligibility
sections.body: You must be at least 18 years old and able to form a legally binding contract in your jurisdiction to use Escroc. By registering, you confirm that this is accurate.

sections.title: Account & Verification (KYC)
sections.body: You are responsible for keeping your login credentials secure. Certain transaction limits and features require identity verification, and Escroc may request additional documentation at any time to comply with anti-fraud and anti-money-laundering obligations.

sections.title: Escrow Service
sections.body: Escroc acts as a neutral third party holding funds until both the buyer and seller fulfill the terms they agreed to. We do not guarantee the quality, legality, or delivery of goods and services exchanged between users — our role is limited to holding and releasing funds per the escrow terms.

sections.title: Prohibited Use
sections.body: You may not use Escroc for illegal transactions, money laundering, fraud, or any activity prohibited by applicable law. We reserve the right to suspend or terminate accounts found in violation, and to report suspicious activity to the relevant authorities.

sections.title: Fees & Currency Exchange
sections.body: Fees for deposits, withdrawals, escrow transactions, and currency exchange are displayed before you confirm any action. Exchange rates are updated periodically and may vary at the time of the transaction.

sections.title: Limitation of Liability
sections.body: Escroc is not liable for indirect, incidental, or consequential damages arising from your use of the platform, including losses caused by third-party payment providers or blockchain network delays outside our control.

sections.title: Changes to These Terms
sections.body: We may revise these Terms from time to time. Continued use of Escroc after changes are posted constitutes acceptance of the updated Terms.

faqPage.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faqPage.subtitle: Answers to common questions about escrow, payments, and security on Escroc.

items.q: How does escrow work on Escroc?
items.a: Escroc holds the buyer's payment securely until both sides confirm the deal is complete, then releases the funds to the seller — protecting both parties from fraud.

items.q: What currencies and payment methods are supported?
items.a: You can fund your wallet using cards, bank transfers, and native cryptocurrencies, and exchange between fiat and crypto wallets directly from your dashboard.

items.q: Do I need to complete KYC?
items.a: Some transaction limits and features require identity verification. You can submit your documents from Dashboard → KYC, and most reviews complete within 24 hours.

items.q: What happens if there's a dispute?
items.a: Either party can raise a dispute from the escrow's conversation page. Our team reviews the evidence and messages exchanged before deciding how funds are released.

items.q: How long does a payment take to arrive?
items.a: Card and bank payments are typically confirmed within minutes to a few hours; crypto payments are credited once the transaction reaches the required number of confirmations on-chain.

items.q: Can I use Escroc as both a buyer and a seller?
items.a: Yes — you can switch between the Buyer and Seller view anytime from your dashboard without creating a separate account.
Yes. Card payments are processed through PCI-DSS compliant gateways, and sensitive data is encrypted both in transit and at rest.
Fees vary by payment gateway and currency exchange rate, and are always shown before you confirm a deposit, withdrawal, or exchange.

items.q: Can I cancel an escrow after creating it?
items.a: An escrow can be cancelled before the counterparty pays. Once payment is confirmed, it can only be resolved through release or a dispute.
Open a ticket from Dashboard → Support, or email support@escroc.com — our team typically responds within one business day.
